reviews.author: Jason Gunthorpe
reviews.summary: reviewer questioned why a writable pte for shadow-stack mappings is rejected, noting that only DMA should be restricted from writing to it; he also asked about x86 specifics and suggested adding more explanation
reviews.raw_body:
I'm not sure I understand this? The pte is writable but you don't want
only DMA to write to it?

Is there something special on x86 that makes the shadow stack pte
non-writable by the CPU?

A few more words here would help

Regardless, this seems reasonable to me, there is no use case to
write to the shadow stack..

Reviewed-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>

Jason

reviews.author: Jason Gunthorpe
reviews.summary: Reviewer Jason Gunthorpe noted that pte_write() incorrectly returns true for shadow-stack PTEs, which can lead to devices gaining write access when they shouldn't, and suggested introducing a new function like pte_real_write() to accurately report the write bit.
reviews.raw_body:
Bah, it's not writable at all. The CPU PTE has write disabled and
someone thought it was a good idea to make pte_write() return true
because the CPU allows writes through a special instruction on this
special PTE? So now all the places like this think its writable, when
it really isn't.

You could also fix this by having something like pte_real_write() or
whatever that doesn't lie about the write bit in the PTE :|

The patch is still fine, in that it matches what everything else does,
but I'd include these details someplace..

Jason

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that on x86, shadow-stack PTEs have their write bit clear but pte_write() reports them writable due to special instructions, allowing GPU access and potential corruption of return addresses or bypassing protection; requested rejecting shadow-stack VMAs in hmm_vma_walk_test() including read access
reviews.raw_body:
How does this look for an altered changelog?

: On x86, a shadow-stack PTE has its ordinary write bit clear.  The CPU
: rejects ordinary stores to it, but pte_write() reports it writable because
: shadow-stack instructions can write it.  HMM consequently sets
: HMM_PFN_WRITE, which Nouveau turns into ordinary GPU write permission.  A
: process with GPU access can then overwrite its own shadow stack,
: potentially corrupting return addresses or bypassing that protection.
: 
: Reject shadow-stack VMAs in hmm_vma_walk_test(), including read access.  A
: requested fault returns -EFAULT; a snapshot records HMM_PFN_ERROR.

2026-11-13.patch_summary: This patch rejects shadow-stack mappings in the Heterogeneous Memory Management (HMM) module to prevent devices from gaining write access to user-space shadow stacks on x86 architectures.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (Meta)
reviews.summary: Questioned the design choice of rejecting shadow-stack mappings, suggesting it's a 'bizarre' decision. Proposed renaming pte_write() to pte_fake_write().

reviews.author: David Hildenbrand (Arm)
reviews.summary: Clarified that pte_write() is writable by hardware, and core-mm code should not write to random PTEs. Suggested using GUP for proper handling.

2026-11-14.patch_summary: The patch aims to reject shadow-stack mappings, but the design choice is questioned.
